title: In de supermarkt
subtitle: Groceries and plurals
intro: In this lesson you learn to name common groceries in Dutch. You can ask where something is in the supermarket and understand the answer. You also learn how to make Dutch plurals with -en and -s.

words.note: As a product usually uncountable; **de kazen** = types of cheese.
Often used as a mass word; plural **de groenten**.
As meat usually uncountable; **de kippen** = chickens.
**De vis** can be food or a fish; **de vissen** = fish (animals).

example.en: I have a pack of milk.
I have a bottle of milk.
I have a tin of fish.

words.forms: ik zoek, jij zoekt, wij zoeken

example.en: I am looking for the cheese.

words.forms: ik vind, jij vindt, wij vinden
ik sta, jij staat, wij staan
words.note: Use **staan** for things standing on a shelf.

words.forms: ik lig, jij ligt, wij liggen

phrases.note: Use **staan** for things standing on a shelf.

phrases.en: I am looking for the bread.

grammar.title: Plurals: -en and -s
grammar.explanation: Most Dutch nouns make the plural with **-en**: **het boek** -> **de boeken**, **de tomaat** -> **de tomaten**. If a noun ends in an unstressed **-el, -er, -en, -em** or **-je**, add **-s**: **de tafel** -> **de tafels**, **de appel** -> **de appels**. Learn the plural together with the article.

examples.nl: Het boek is duur. De boeken zijn duur.
examples.en: The book is expensive. The books are expensive.

examples.nl: De appel is lekker. De appels zijn lekker.
examples.en: The apple is tasty. The apples are tasty.

grammar.tip: Say the plural aloud: **appel -> appels**, **tomaat -> tomaten**.

grammar.title: Spelling in plurals
grammar.explanation: When you add **-en**, the spelling can change. A long vowel stays long: **de tomaat** -> **de tomaten**, **de banaan** -> **de bananen**. A short vowel needs a double consonant: **de kat** -> **de katten**, **de kip** -> **de kippen**, **het blik** -> **de blikken**. Listen carefully to the vowel sound.

rows: long a stays long; one a before -en
long a stays long; one a before -en

examples.nl: De tomaat is lekker. De tomaten zijn lekker.
examples.en: The tomato is tasty. The tomatoes are tasty.

examples.nl: Het blik is duur. De blikken zijn duur.
examples.en: The tin is expensive. The tins are expensive.

grammar.tip: Say the plural aloud: **tomaat -> tomaten**, **kat -> katten**.

grammar.title: All plurals take de
grammar.explanation: All Dutch plurals take **de**. A **het**-word becomes **de** in the plural: **het brood** -> **de broden**, **het ei** -> **de eieren**. A **de**-word keeps **de**: **de appel** -> **de appels**.

examples.nl: Het brood is duur. De broden zijn duur.
examples.en: The bread is expensive. The loaves are expensive.

examples.nl: Het ei is lekker. De eieren zijn lekker.
examples.en: The egg is tasty. The eggs are tasty.

grammar.tip: If the singular has **het**, the plural has **de**.

dialogue.title: Waar is de kaas?
dialogue.setting: In a supermarket in Utrecht. Sanne is looking for cheese, eggs and bread.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.en: I am looking for the cheese.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.nl: De kaas staat daar, bij de melk.
lines.en: The cheese is there, by the milk.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Dank u wel. En waar liggen de eieren?
lines.en: Thank you. And where are the eggs?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.nl: De eieren liggen bij de melk.
lines.en: The eggs are by the milk.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.nl: Ja, het brood ligt bij de kassa.
lines.en: Yes, the bread is at the checkout.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.nl: De yoghurt staat bij de melk.
lines.en: The yoghurt is by the milk.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Ik heb een pak melk en een fles jus d'orange.
lines.en: I have a pack of milk and a bottle of orange juice.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Ja, dat is alles. Dank u wel.
lines.en: Yes, that is all. Thank you.

culture.title: Bring your own bag
culture.text: In the Netherlands, you often pay a small amount for a plastic bag at the shop. Since 2016, Dutch shops are not allowed to give free plastic bags. Many people bring their own bag or buy a reusable one. At the supermarket you usually pack your groceries yourself at the checkout.

summary: Most plurals add **-en**; after unstressed **-el, -er, -en, -em, -je** add **-s**.
Use **staan** for things standing and **liggen** for things lying.
Ask **Waar staat...?**, **Waar ligt...?**, **Waar staan...?** or **Waar liggen...?** to find products.
